summary: Consolidated candidate PR https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/2738 with corrections for the concrete counterexamples reported by review PR https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/2803. Startup now supplies the current code revision and normalized runtime environment to the resolver, stale records fail closed, and a report's feasible flag cannot authorize a plan whose parallel-degree product differs from num_gpus.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction against candidate commit 1a422dd3f344dd098af11e25a4bad951bd9daf62: stale-environment support was absent and an internally impossible feasible plan was selected; 4 failed, 10 passed. Raw output: failing-before.log.
Passing-after resolver, startup integration, explicit-precedence, compatibility, and singleton behavior: 214 passed and 67 subtests passed. Raw output: compatibility-after.log.
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, and policy hooks for all corrected source/test/documentation files. Raw output: pre-commit.log.

Read-only environment evidence: Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2.26015, one visible AMD Instinct MI350X, and the exact normalized environment emitted by the advisor. This is not counted as feature execution. Raw output: environment.log.

gpu_evidence: A GPU was detected only by a read-only environment probe. No diffusion model weights, model-specific quality reference, or multi-GPU allocation were available, so no serving/calibration workload or independent numerical check was run.
remaining_limitations: The original feature's isolated calibration runner, full benchmark/instrumentation protocol, model accuracy gate execution, startup metrics, and separately launched pool routing remain outside this bounded correction.

No end-to-end diffusion calibration matrix, model semantic qualification, or multi-rank topology initialization was run because the required weights/reference and multi-GPU allocation were unavailable.

Runtime checking can enforce only intrinsic plan legality at this early startup stage; model-specific TP/SP/FSDP capabilities continue to require the existing later pipeline validation and calibrated evidence.
